content.title: About
content.content: Light wine is a fermented beverage made from white grapes or from red grapes that have been pressed to remove the skins. It features a pale golden or straw‑yellow color, delicate fruit aromas, and moderate acidity. Light wine is often served chilled as an aperitif or paired with light dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Light wine can be dry, off‑dry, or semi‑sweet depending on residual sugar levels.
The oldest known sample of light wine dates back to 6000 BC and was discovered in Georgia.
The name “Chardonnay” derives from the French word “shard,” referring to the wine’s characteristic earthy notes.
Many light wines are aged in oak barrels, imparting hints of vanilla and spice.
In Italy, certain light wines are called “Vin Santo” and are used in cooking.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds in wine help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Moderate consumption of light wine is associated with improved lipid profiles and reduced risk of ischemic heart disease.

items.title: Rich in polyphenols
items.content: Polyphenols may enhance endothelial function of blood vessels.

items.title: Moderate alcohol level
items.content: Small amounts of alcohol can have a relaxing effect and improve mood.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Wine contains modest amounts of vitamins B1, B2, and B6, which are involved in metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to dependence, liver damage, and other health issues.

items.title: Sulfite allergy
items.content: Sulfites used as preservatives may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain drugs, such as sedatives.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Light wine provides about 80 kcal per 100 ml, which should be considered in weight management.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit or avoid alcohol entirely.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: Serve light wine chilled (8‑12 °C). It pairs well with seafood, light salads, soft cheeses, and fruit‑based desserts. For tasting, pour a small amount into a glass, let it breathe for a few minutes, then assess aroma and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place on its side to keep the cork moist. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days, sealing the bottle tightly and refrigerating.
